## Responsibility

Reads a Java repository into core's model without a JDK and without running the build (ADR-0107): Java sources through web-tree-sitter and tree-sitter-java's WebAssembly grammar (declarations, members, annotations with their arguments, router calls), Maven and Gradle builds (modules, source roots, dependencies, the Java version), descriptors (web.xml, persistence.xml, Spring XML, `application*.properties|yml`), the import edges and symbols of `.java` files for the shared graph, and the build's modules as workspace packages. It decides no framework fact: endpoints, entities, beans and configuration are core's domain.

## Invariants

- A file with a syntax error keeps what it declares and says where it broke [[cite: packages/plugin-java/src/tree-sitter-java-parser.ts:197 | "} else if (!error && (type === \"ERROR\" || cursor.nodeIsMissing)) {"]].
- A library type is external as `java:<package>`, never an npm name [[cite: packages/plugin-java/src/java-import-analyzer.ts:202 | "return { type: \"external\", name: `java:${pkg || specifier}` };"]].
- A Java file's fingerprint carries the type index's digest: its edges depend on the other files [[cite: packages/plugin-java/src/java-import-analyzer.ts:118 | "return `${Bun.hash(content).toString(16)}:${this.types().digest}`;"]].

## Allowed dependencies

`@metator/core`, `web-tree-sitter`, `tree-sitter-java` (its `.wasm` only), `saxes` and `yaml`. No other plugin; the runtime wires it and hands it the grammar's files.

## Pitfalls

- web-tree-sitter starts asynchronously: the synchronous `ImportAnalyzer` reads imports with the tokenizer (`java-lexer.ts`), not the parser.
- A Gradle script is code: dependencies, source sets and the Java version are read only when written simply.
- Unknown `${...}` placeholders stay as written; a parent POM outside the repository gives no properties.
